newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-WALLABIES WITHSTAND IRISH ONSLAUGHT TO STAY UNBEATEN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WALLABIES WITHSTAND IRISH ONSLAUGHT TO STAY UNBEATEN.

text.p: Australia remained on course for a Celtic grand slam after weathering a furious Irish onslaught in bitterly cold conditions at Lansdowne Road on Saturday.

The Wallabies trailed 12-9 with 13 minutes left before finally emerging with a 22-12 win which extended their unbeaten European tour record to nine matches and revived memories of their 1991 World Cup quarter-final victory on the same ground.
The Irish, revitalised under the command of hooker Keith Wood, threatened for long periods to cause a major upset which seemed impossible last week in the wake of a 40-25 loss to Western Samoa.

But a halftime lead of 9-6 proved an insufficient cushion when they turned to face the wind in the second-half and Australian full-back Matt Burke coolly dug his side out of trouble with five penalties and a conversion of David Knox's 78th minute try.

Burke, who scored 19 points in the 29-19 win over Scotland a fortnight ago, landed two killer blows from close to the halfway line to put his side ahead 15-12 with 10 minutes to go although Ireland still had their chances.
Fly-half Paul Burke, who had kicked all four of his previous penalty efforts, sliced a fifth attempt which would have tied the scores again and the Wallabies did not allow him another chance.
There had been a subdued mood around the ground before kick- off which suggested the heavy defeat by the Samoans was still weighing heavily on Irish minds.
The reshaped Irish pack had other ideas and although Burke put the Wallabies ahead with a second-minute penalty, the bulk of the first-half action took place in Australian territory.
Ignoring the loss of full-back Jim Staples, forced off with a hand injury after only 13 minutes, the home forwards drove at their opponents with relish and fully deserved to be ahead at the interval.
Turning to face the wind, though, there was always the suspicion that Ireland might be more vulnerable and their slender lead was gone within two minutes of the restart.

Even the loss of skipper John Eales in the 64th minute did not deter the Wallabies and by the time Knox dived gleefully under the posts, the prospect of a first Irish victory over Australia since 1979 had already gone.
Lansdowne Road was the venue of one of rugby's most exciting finales in 1991 as the Wallabies scored in injury-time to deny the Irish a place in the World Cup semifinals.

Having now seen off the Scots and Irish, the Wallabies final test of the tour is against Wales in Cardiff next Sunday, although they will also meet an international-strength Barbarians team at Twickenham next month.

Ireland - 15-Jim Staples (16-Maurice Field, 13th); 14-James Topping, 13-Jonathan Bell, 12-Mark McCall, 11-Dominic Crotty; 10-Paul Burke, 9-Steve McIvor; 8-Anthony Foley, 7-Denis McBride, 6-David Corkery, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Gabriel Fulcher, 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Keith Wood (captain), 1-Nick Popplewell.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Jason Little, 13-Daniel Herbert, 12-Tim Horan, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan; 8-Michael Brial, 7-David Wilson, 6-Daniel Manu, 5-John Eales (captain) (19-Brett Robinson, 65th), 4-Warwick Waugh, 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Dan Crowley.
